      "content": "Corporate training builds shared understanding. Ministry-specific training builds specialized competence. Each ministry team needs customized training that prepares them for their unique responsibilities.

This article outlines the training requirements for each key ministry area.

---

## The Training Principle

Every ministry team needs training in three areas:

| Area | Question Answered |
|------|------------------|
| **Philosophy** | Why do we do this ministry? |
| **Procedures** | How do we execute our responsibilities? |
| **Practice** | Have we rehearsed until we're confident? |

Skip any of these, and teams arrive at Launch Sunday either unmotivated (missing philosophy), confused (missing procedures), or unprepared (missing practice).

<Callout type="important">
  Ministry-specific training should be 90-100% complete by the time you 
  reach the final 3-4 weeks before launch. That final window is for 
  integration, not foundational training.
</Callout>

---

## Worship & Production Team

The worship and production team owns the entire Sunday morning experience from a technical and artistic standpoint.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Theology of Worship** | Why we worship, what worship accomplishes |
| **Service Philosophy** | What we're trying to create on Sunday morning |
| **Excellence and Accessibility** | High quality without being intimidating |
| **Team Character** | Humility, preparation, servant hearts |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Service Flow** | Order of service, transitions, timing |
| **Rehearsal Protocol** | When, how long, what to cover |
| **Sound Setup** | Board configuration, mic placement, mixing |
| **Video/Lighting** | Projection, slides, lighting cues |
| **Stage Setup** | Instrument placement, cables, stands |
| **Communication** | In-ear cues, hand signals, contingency plans |

### Practice Requirements

- Multiple full rehearsals with all elements
- Pre-Launch Services as dress rehearsals
- Walk-through of set-up and tear-down procedures
- Practice handling equipment failures and contingencies

---

## Children's Ministry Team

Children's Ministry requires extensive training due to safety requirements and the specialized nature of teaching children.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Why Children's Ministry Matters** | Impact on families, discipleship begins early |
| **Ministry Philosophy** | How we approach teaching and caring for children |
| **Age-Appropriate Faith Development** | What kids can understand at each stage |
| **Partnership with Parents** | Supporting, not replacing, parental discipleship |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Check-In Process** | Registration, name tags, security codes |
| **Safety Protocols** | Adult-to-child ratios, bathroom procedures, never alone |
| **Classroom Management** | Handling behavior, engaging activities |
| **Curriculum Execution** | How to teach the lesson effectively |
| **Allergy and Medical** | Identifying allergies, medication policies |
| **Emergency Procedures** | Fire, medical emergency, security threat |
| **Parent Communication** | Pickup procedures, incident reports |

### Practice Requirements

- Full walk-through of check-in process
- Role-play of common scenarios (crying child, bathroom needs, behavior issues)
- Practice with all equipment (check-in system, pagers, etc.)
- Pre-Launch Service with real children

<Callout type="warning">
  Children's Ministry training is non-negotiable. Every volunteer must 
  complete background checks and safety training before serving. No exceptions.
</Callout>

---

## Facilities Team

The facilities team transforms a rented space into a welcoming worship environment and returns it to its original state every week.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **First Impressions** | The building speaks before anyone does |
| **Stewardship** | Caring for what we've been given |
| **Relationship with Facility Owner** | Being excellent tenants |
| **Team Culture** | Serving together, having fun |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Set-Up Sequence** | What gets set up first, workflow optimization |
| **Room Configuration** | Seating arrangement, stage setup, signage |
| **Equipment Handling** | Proper care of sound, video, lighting gear |
| **Storage Procedures** | How to load, organize, and secure equipment |
| **Tear-Down Sequence** | Efficient breakdown, facility restoration |
| **Parking and Signage** | Directing guests, outdoor setup |
| **Trailer Loading** | Maximizing space, securing equipment |

### Practice Requirements

- Full set-up and tear-down rehearsal (timed)
- In-Service Training Day with all equipment
- Walk-through of every storage and setup location
- Pre-Launch Services as full practice

---

## Assimilation Team

The assimilation team owns the guest experience from arrival through follow-up.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Why Guests Matter** | Every guest is someone God brought |
| **The Guest Experience** | Seeing Sunday through a newcomer's eyes |
| **From Guest to Family** | The pathway from first visit to belonging |
| **Warmth Without Weirdness** | Being friendly without being overwhelming |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Greeter Positioning** | Where to stand, what to say |
| **Guest Identification** | Spotting first-time guests |
| **Registration Process** | Connection cards, Friendship Registers |
| **Guest Reception Area** | What it is, how it works |
| **Usher Responsibilities** | Seating, offering, assistance |
| **Database Entry** | Entering guest information accurately |
| **Follow-Up Process** | Who contacts, when, how |

### Practice Requirements

- Role-play of greeting scenarios
- Practice with registration systems
- Walk-through of entire guest pathway
- Pre-Launch Service with team members acting as guests

<Callout type="tip">
  Have team members visit another church anonymously and report on their 
  experience. Nothing teaches the guest perspective like being a guest.
</Callout>

---

## Small Group Team

Small group leaders receive dedicated training through Small Group 101, but the broader small group team also needs coordination training.

### Coordination Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Group Launch Strategy** | How and when groups will launch |
| **Sign-Up Process** | How people join groups |
| **Assignment Process** | How people are placed in groups |
| **Leader Support** | How coaches support leaders |
| **Reporting and Communication** | Attendance, concerns, needs |

### See Also

- [Small Group 101](/wiki/training/small-group-101) for leader-specific training

## Promotion Team

The promotion team owns marketing and communication before, during, and after launch.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Why Promotion Matters** | Getting the word out to reach people |
| **Brand and Message** | What we communicate and how |
| **Excellence in Communication** | Quality reflects the message |
| **Stewardship of Resources** | Maximum impact, appropriate spending |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Pre-Launch Promotion** | Timeline and channels |
| **Launch Day Documentation** | Photo and video capture |
| **Social Media** | Platforms, posting schedule, voice |
| **Print Materials** | Design, production, distribution |
| **Website Management** | Updates, content, accuracy |
| **Email Communication** | Lists, frequency, content |

### Practice Requirements

- Dry run of all promotion channels
- Test all digital systems (website, email, social)
- Practice video/photo capture during Pre-Launch Services

---

## Prayer Team

The prayer team undergirds everything with intercession.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Theology of Prayer** | Why prayer matters, how it works |
| **Corporate Prayer** | Praying together as a body |
| **Intercessory Prayer** | Standing in the gap for others |
| **Prayer and the Launch** | Covering the launch in prayer |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Pre-Service Prayer** | When, where, who |
| **Prayer During Service** | Designated prayer space, rotation |
| **Prayer Requests** | Collection, confidentiality, follow-up |
| **Corporate Prayer Gatherings** | Format, frequency, leadership |
| **Communication** | Sharing requests, updates, answers |

---

## Technology Team

The technology team handles digital infrastructure and technical support.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Technology as Tool** | Serving the mission, not showing off |
| **Reliability** | Systems that work every time |
| **Appropriate Investment** | Wise use of resources |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Website Management** | Updates, content management |
| **Presentation Software** | Slides, lyrics, announcements |
| **Database Systems** | Guest management, reporting |
| **Troubleshooting** | Common problems and solutions |
| **Backup Plans** | What to do when systems fail |

---

## Administration Team

The administration team handles finance and church operations.

### Philosophy Training

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Biblical Stewardship** | Managing God's resources faithfully |
| **Financial Integrity** | Above reproach in all things |
| **Confidentiality** | Protecting sensitive information |

### Procedures Training

| Area | What to Cover |
|------|---------------|
| **Offering Collection** | Secure handling of cash and checks |
| **Counting Procedures** | Two-person rule, documentation |
| **Recording and Reporting** | Database entry, reports |
| **Disbursements** | Approval process, check signing |
| **Contribution Statements** | Frequency, accuracy |

<Callout type="important">
  Financial procedures must be established and followed from day one. 
  Sloppy financial practices early create problems that compound over time.
</Callout>

---

## Training Delivery

### Who Trains Each Team?

| Team | Primary Trainer |
|------|-----------------|
| Worship & Production | Worship Leader |
| Children's Ministry | Children's Ministry Leader |
| Facilities | Facilities Leader |
| Assimilation | Assimilation Leader + Senior Pastor |
| Small Groups | Small Group Leader + Senior Pastor |
| Promotion | Promotion Leader |
| Prayer | Prayer Leader + Senior Pastor |
| Technology | Technology Leader |
| Administration | Senior Pastor + Financial Leader |

### Training Schedule

Build ministry training into your Phase 3 calendar:

1. **Early Phase 3** — Philosophy training for all teams
2. **Mid Phase 3** — Procedures training by team
3. **Late Phase 3** — Practice through Pre-Launch Services
4. **Final Weeks** — Refinement and integration

      "content": "Peak Performance is a three-session training series that serves as your church's membership class. Every Launch Team member should complete this series before Launch Sunday—and it becomes the pathway for new members after launch.

The series accomplishes two critical goals: it ensures alignment around your church's DNA, and it creates a clear pathway for commitment.

---

## Why Peak Performance?

New churches often assume alignment exists because enthusiasm is high. But enthusiasm without understanding leads to confusion and conflict later. Peak Performance creates **informed commitment**.

<Callout type="insight">
  People can't commit to what they don't understand. Peak Performance gives 
  them the clarity needed to commit wholeheartedly—or to recognize they're 
  not the right fit.
</Callout>

### What Peak Performance Accomplishes

| Session | Outcome |
|---------|---------|
| **Peak Performance I** | Understanding of vision and values |
| **Peak Performance II** | Alignment on beliefs and doctrine |
| **Peak Performance III** | Clarity on commitment and next steps |

---

## Peak Performance I: Vision, Mission, and Values

**Purpose:** Help participants understand what this church is about and where it's going.

This session answers the fundamental questions: *Why does this church exist? What makes it distinct? Where is it headed?*

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **The Story** | How this church plant came to be |
| **Vision** | The preferred future you're pursuing |
| **Mission** | The specific work God has called you to |
| **Core Values** | The non-negotiables that guide decisions |
| **The 4 Pillars** | Your theological foundation |
| **Worship/Walk/Work** | Your discipleship model |

### Session Flow

1. **Welcome and introductions** — Create a warm, inviting environment
2. **The Story** — Share the journey that led to this church plant
3. **Vision and Mission** — Cast a clear picture of what you're building
4. **Core Values** — Explain each value with practical examples
5. **4 Pillars Overview** — Introduce the theological foundation
6. **Discipleship Model** — Explain Worship/Walk/Work
7. **Q&A** — Address questions and concerns
8. **Preview of Session II** — Set expectations for next week

<Callout type="tip">
  Use visuals. PowerPoint, handouts, and banners help people grasp and 
  remember key concepts. The 4 Pillars and Worship/Walk/Work especially 
  benefit from visual representation.
</Callout>

---

## Peak Performance II: Beliefs and Doctrine

**Purpose:** Ensure alignment on what this church believes and teaches.

Doctrinal clarity prevents future conflict. This session walks through your statement of faith and explains how your beliefs shape ministry practice.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Statement of Faith** | Walk through each doctrinal point |
| **The Gospel** | Clear articulation of the good news |
| **The Bible** | Your view of Scripture's authority |
| **The Church** | Theology of the local church |
| **Baptism and Communion** | Your practice of the ordinances |
| **Church Government** | Elder leadership and how decisions are made |
| **Distinctives** | What sets this church apart doctrinally |

### Session Flow

1. **Review** — Brief recap of Session I
2. **Why Doctrine Matters** — Connect beliefs to everyday life
3. **Statement of Faith** — Systematic walk-through
4. **Gospel Presentation** — Ensure everyone can articulate the gospel
5. **Church Practices** — Explain baptism, communion, membership
6. **Government Structure** — How the church is led and governed
7. **Q&A** — Address theological questions
8. **Preview of Session III** — Set expectations for commitment discussion

<Callout type="important">
  This session may surface disagreements. That's healthy. Better to discover 
  misalignment now than after someone is serving in leadership.
</Callout>

---

## Peak Performance III: Commitment and Next Steps

**Purpose:** Call participants to clear commitment and explain what membership involves.

This session moves from information to invitation. After two sessions of learning, participants are asked to decide: *Will you commit?*

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **The Call to Commitment** | Why formal commitment matters |
| **Membership Expectations** | What's expected of members |
| **Serving Opportunities** | Ministry teams and how to get involved |
| **Giving** | The role of generosity in the life of a believer |
| **Small Groups** | The importance of community |
| **Next Steps** | How to formalize membership |
| **Commitment Card** | Walking through and signing the commitment |

### Session Flow

1. **Review** — Brief recap of Sessions I and II
2. **The Call** — Biblical basis for church commitment
3. **Expectations** — Clear explanation of what membership involves
4. **Serving** — Overview of ministry teams and spiritual gifts
5. **Generosity** — Teaching on biblical stewardship
6. **Community** — The role of small groups
7. **Commitment Time** — Invitation to sign commitment cards
8. **Celebration** — Welcome new members, pray over them
9. **Next Steps** — What happens after commitment

<Callout type="tip">
  Don't rush the commitment moment. Give people time to read, reflect, and 
  ask questions. Pressured commitment creates shallow members.
</Callout>

---

## Logistics and Format

### Session Length

Plan for 90 minutes per session:
- 60 minutes of content
- 15 minutes for Q&A
- 15 minutes for fellowship and follow-up

### Scheduling Options

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| **Three consecutive weeks** | Momentum, easy to track | Requires three-week commitment |
| **One intensive day** | Complete in one sitting | Long day, less reflection time |
| **Monthly rotation** | Flexible entry points | Takes longer to complete |

For the Launch Team, three consecutive weeks works best. After launch, consider a monthly rotation for ongoing membership.

### Materials Needed

- [ ] PowerPoint or slides for each session
- [ ] Handouts summarizing key content
- [ ] Statement of faith document
- [ ] Commitment cards
- [ ] Ministry team descriptions and sign-up sheets
- [ ] Small group information
- [ ] Name tags and sign-in sheets

---

## Running Peak Performance for Your Launch Team

For your Launch Team, Peak Performance serves as both training and commitment formalization. Schedule the series early enough in Phase 3 that everyone completes it well before launch.

### Recommendations

1. **Require attendance** — Make clear this is expected of all Launch Team members
2. **Provide make-up options** — Offer alternative times for those who miss sessions
3. **Use it as alignment check** — Pay attention to questions and concerns raised
4. **Celebrate completion** — Recognize those who complete the series

<Callout type="warning">
  If someone in your Launch Team resists completing Peak Performance, that's 
  a signal worth exploring. Commitment to the process reflects commitment to 
  the mission.
</Callout>

---

## After Launch

Peak Performance becomes your ongoing membership pathway. New guests who want to join complete the series and sign commitment cards just like your Launch Team did.

### Ongoing Schedule

Most churches offer Peak Performance:
- Monthly (one session per month, rotating)
- Quarterly (three-week intensive each quarter)
- On demand (when enough new people are ready)

Choose the rhythm that fits your context and growth pace.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"Him we proclaim, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, 
  that we may present everyone mature in Christ."* — Colossians 1:28
</Callout>

      "content": "Small groups are where discipleship happens. Sunday services gather the church, but small groups grow the church. Every healthy church plant needs trained small group leaders ready to shepherd people in community.

Small Group 101 is your training course for equipping those leaders.

---

## Why Small Groups Matter

Small groups accomplish what Sunday services cannot:

| Sunday Service | Small Group |
|----------------|-------------|
| Inspires many at once | Develops individuals deeply |
| One-way communication | Interactive discussion |
| Anonymous attendance possible | Accountability and relationship |
| Surface-level connection | Genuine community |

<Callout type="insight">
  Sunday services can draw a crowd, but small groups build a church. 
  Without healthy small groups, growth becomes a mile wide and an inch deep.
</Callout>

A church of 100 without small groups has 100 loosely connected individuals. A church of 100 with strong small groups has 10 families deeply invested in each other's lives.

---

## Small Group 101 Objectives

By the end of this training, leaders should be able to:

1. **Articulate** the philosophy and purpose of small groups
2. **Facilitate** engaging group discussions
3. **Shepherd** group members through life's challenges
4. **Multiply** by developing apprentice leaders
5. **Execute** the logistical requirements of leading a group

---

## Session 1: Philosophy and Purpose

**Goal:** Leaders understand *why* small groups exist and how they fit into the church's discipleship model.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Biblical Foundation** | Acts 2:42-47, one-anothers, early church model |
| **Discipleship Model** | Where groups fit in Worship/Walk/Work |
| **The Ministry Funnel** | How people move from guest to group |
| **Group Purpose** | Community, growth, care, mission |
| **Expectations** | What's expected of leaders and members |

### Key Concepts

**The "Walk" in Worship/Walk/Work**

Small groups are the "Walk" component—where believers walk together in community, growing in Christlikeness through relationship.

**The Three Purposes of Small Groups**

1. **Connect** — Build authentic relationships
2. **Grow** — Study Scripture and apply it together
3. **Serve** — Care for one another and reach outward

<Callout type="tip">
  Help leaders see that their group isn't just a Bible study—it's a 
  community with a mission. Groups that only study together eventually 
  stagnate. Groups that serve together thrive.
</Callout>

---

## Session 2: Facilitation Skills

**Goal:** Leaders can guide engaging, transformative group discussions.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Facilitator vs. Teacher** | Drawing out vs. pouring in |
| **Question Types** | Open, closed, application, personal |
| **Discussion Dynamics** | Handling talkers, drawing out quiet members |
| **Creating Safety** | Confidentiality, vulnerability, grace |
| **Time Management** | Balancing fellowship, study, and prayer |

### The Art of Asking Questions

Good facilitators ask questions that open conversation, not shut it down.

| Instead of... | Ask... |
|---------------|--------|
| "The answer is grace, right?" | "What stands out to you in this passage?" |
| "Don't you agree that...?" | "How have you seen this play out in your life?" |
| "Does anyone have questions?" | "What questions does this raise for you?" |

### Handling Common Challenges

| Challenge | Response |
|-----------|----------|
| **The talker** | "Great insight. Let's hear from someone who hasn't shared yet." |
| **The silent member** | "Sarah, I'd love to hear your perspective on this." |
| **The tangent** | "That's interesting. Let's table that for after group." |
| **The debater** | "Good question. What do others think?" |
| **The advice-giver** | "Instead of solutions, let's just listen and pray." |

<Callout type="warning">
  New leaders often over-prepare content and under-prepare for group 
  dynamics. The best content means nothing if the discussion falls flat. 
  Spend as much time preparing to facilitate as preparing the material.
</Callout>

---

## Session 3: Shepherding Skills

**Goal:** Leaders can care for group members through life's challenges.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Shepherd's Heart** | Caring for people, not just managing meetings |
| **One-on-One Connection** | Meeting with members outside of group |
| **Crisis Response** | How to respond when life falls apart |
| **Appropriate Referral** | Knowing when to involve pastors or professionals |
| **Prayer Ministry** | Praying for and with group members |

### The Shepherding Rhythm

Effective small group leaders maintain connection between meetings:

| Frequency | Activity |
|-----------|----------|
| **Weekly** | Check-in texts or calls |
| **Monthly** | One-on-one coffee or meal with a member |
| **As needed** | Crisis response and hospital visits |
| **Ongoing** | Prayer for each member by name |

### Knowing Your Limits

Small group leaders are not counselors, therapists, or pastors. Train leaders to recognize when situations require referral:

- Mental health crises
- Marriage counseling needs
- Addiction issues
- Abuse situations
- Complex theological questions

<Callout type="important">
  The goal is not to equip leaders to handle every situation—it's to equip 
  them to recognize what they can handle and what requires the Senior Pastor 
  or professional help.
</Callout>

---

## Session 4: Multiplication and Apprenticeship

**Goal:** Leaders understand how to develop future leaders and multiply their group.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Why Multiply** | Kingdom growth, leadership development, fresh energy |
| **The Apprentice Model** | Identifying and developing potential leaders |
| **Multiplication Pathway** | How groups grow and birth new groups |
| **Overcoming Resistance** | Addressing fear of change |
| **Healthy Endings** | Celebrating and transitioning well |

### The Apprentice Pathway

1. **Identify** — Look for the "3 C's": Character, Competence, Chemistry
2. **Invite** — Ask them to consider leadership
3. **Include** — Bring them into planning and decision-making
4. **Instruct** — Teach them through explanation and observation
5. **Release** — Gradually hand over responsibilities
6. **Launch** — Send them to lead their own group

### When to Multiply

Groups should consider multiplication when:
- Size consistently exceeds 12-15 people
- An apprentice is ready to lead
- The group has been together 12-18 months
- Energy is high and momentum is strong

<Callout type="tip">
  Multiplication is easier when it's expected from the beginning. Tell new 
  groups on day one: "Our goal is to grow and multiply so more people can 
  experience this kind of community."
</Callout>

---

## Session 5: Logistics and Execution

**Goal:** Leaders understand the practical requirements of running a group.

### Content to Cover

| Topic | Key Points |
|-------|------------|
| **Group Launch** | First meeting essentials |
| **Rhythm and Schedule** | Weekly, bi-weekly, semester-based |
| **Location and Hospitality** | Creating a welcoming environment |
| **Curriculum Selection** | Choosing and preparing studies |
| **Communication** | Keeping members informed |
| **Reporting** | Attendance, pastoral concerns, needs |

### First Meeting Essentials

- [ ] Introductions and icebreakers
- [ ] Establish group expectations (time, confidentiality, participation)
- [ ] Share contact information
- [ ] Preview the curriculum/study
- [ ] Pray together
- [ ] Confirm next meeting details

### Ongoing Administration

| Task | Frequency |
|------|-----------|
| Prepare for meeting | Weekly |
| Send reminders | Weekly |
| Report attendance | Weekly |
| Connect with absent members | After each absence |
| Communicate with coach/pastor | Bi-weekly or as needed |
| Evaluate group health | Quarterly |

---

## Training Format Options

| Format | Duration | Best For |
|--------|----------|----------|
| **Intensive** | Full Saturday (8 hours) | Launch Team training pre-launch |
| **Weekly** | 5 weeks, 90 min each | Ongoing leader development |
| **Cohort** | Monthly over 5 months | New leaders after launch |

For pre-launch, the intensive format works best to get all leaders trained quickly.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, 
  not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging 
  one another."* — Hebrews 10:24-25
</Callout>

      "content": "Once your Core Group transitions to a Launch Team with an established launch date, the mission shifts. Vision Meetings continue, but the primary focus becomes **training and preparation** for Launch Sunday.

This phase is where your team transforms from enthusiastic supporters into equipped servants ready to execute every aspect of a high-impact church launch.

---

## Why Training Matters

A church plant can have the right people, adequate funding, and a great location—but without proper training, Launch Sunday becomes chaotic instead of celebratory. Training accomplishes three essential outcomes:

1. **Competence** — Team members know what to do and how to do it well
2. **Confidence** — Trained teams serve with assurance rather than anxiety
3. **Cohesion** — Training builds teamwork and shared understanding

<Callout type="insight">
  Training doesn't just prepare individuals—it transforms a group of committed 
  people into a unified team that can execute together under pressure.
</Callout>

---

## The Training Framework

Phase 3 training operates on three levels, each serving a distinct purpose:

### Corporate Training

Training delivered to the entire Launch Team together. This builds shared understanding and team unity.

| Program | Purpose | Audience |
|---------|---------|----------|
| Peak Performance Series | Membership and discipleship foundations | All Launch Team members |
| Boot Camp | Intensive discipleship and leadership development | Emerging leaders |

### Ministry Team Training

Specialized training for each ministry area. This builds competence in specific responsibilities.

| Ministry | Training Focus |
|----------|----------------|
| Worship & Production | Service flow, equipment, transitions |
| Children's Ministry | Curriculum, check-in, safety protocols |
| Facilities | Set-up, tear-down, storage procedures |
| Assimilation | Guest process, database, follow-up |
| Small Groups | Leader training, group dynamics, curriculum |

### Observation & Practice

Learning by watching established churches and practicing in your own context.

- Visit partner churches to observe their operations
- Conduct Pre-Launch Services as full rehearsals
- Practice set-up and tear-down until it becomes second nature

---

## Training Programs at a Glance

### Peak Performance Training Series

A three-session membership class that covers the foundational DNA of your church. Every Launch Team member should complete this series.

**Sessions:**
- Peak Performance I — Vision, mission, and values
- Peak Performance II — Beliefs and doctrine
- Peak Performance III — Commitment and next steps

[Learn more about Peak Performance](/wiki/training/peak-performance-training-series)

### Small Group 101

Training for small group leaders that covers the philosophy, mechanics, and leadership skills needed to launch and sustain healthy small groups.

[Learn more about Small Group 101](/wiki/training/small-group-101)

### Boot Camp

An intensive discipleship experience for emerging leaders. Boot Camp goes deeper than Peak Performance, developing the character and skills needed for ministry leadership.

[Learn more about Boot Camp](/wiki/training/boot-camp-overview)

### Ministry-Specific Training

Customized training for each ministry team covering their unique responsibilities, procedures, and standards.

[Learn more about Ministry-Specific Training](/wiki/training/ministry-specific-training)

---

## Training Timeline

Training should be **90-100% complete** by the time you reach the final 3-4 weeks before launch. That final window is for integration and refinement—not foundational training.

| Timeframe | Focus |
|-----------|-------|
| **Early Phase 3** | Corporate training (Peak Performance, Boot Camp) |
| **Mid Phase 3** | Ministry team training begins |
| **Late Phase 3** | Practice, observation visits, refinement |
| **Final 3-4 Weeks** | Pre-Launch Services, integration, final prep |

<Callout type="warning">
  Don't wait until the last minute to train. Rushed training produces anxious 
  teams. Give your people time to learn, practice, and gain confidence.
</Callout>

---

## The Three Meeting Objectives

As your Launch Team meetings become more frequent, they serve three primary objectives:

1. **Inspire** — Continue casting vision through worship, devotional, and prayer
2. **Instill** — Enculturate the team in values, distinctives, and DNA
3. **Inform** — Train the team in their specific responsibilities

[Learn more about Launch Team Meeting Objectives](/wiki/training/launch-team-meeting-objectives)

---

## Training is Discipleship

Never forget that training is ultimately about discipleship. You're not just teaching skills—you're developing people who will serve the Lord and His church for years to come.

The goal isn't a perfect launch. The goal is mature believers equipped for works of service. Launch Sunday is simply the first opportunity to put that equipping into practice.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"And he gave the apostles, the prophets, the evangelists, the shepherds and 
  teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the 
  body of Christ."* — Ephesians 4:11-12
</Callout>

Your job is to equip. Their job is to serve. Together, you build the body of Christ.",

# EveryField Network Intelligence rubric v1

EveryField authored this first portfolio reference on 13 October 2026 under the approved separate-rubric direction. It interprets operational evidence in one exact sending-church/network portfolio. It is separate from the original SME Plant Intelligence rubric and Playbook; those originals are unchanged. This reference now has concrete rules and synthetic expected examples. Model evaluation and production activation are future gates, and no passing application evaluation is claimed.

The complete structured authority is [network-rubric-v1.json](network-rubric-v1.json). There are no weights, health scores or plant rankings. The model phrases supported deterministic rule results and next steps; it does not calculate numbers, create observations, invent testimony or make pastoral judgments.

## Input eligibility and support

A contribution needs a current exact-organization relationship or valid existing grant, health/results `shared_findings` ON, an organization-released PI result where used, and all underlying input-category grants. Health ON never overrides a restricted People/meeting/team/task source. Each pattern at each Region, state/province, Country and Whole portfolio level requires two distinct plants with relevant observed evidence for that specific rule/key. Two directory members, two sharing plants or duplicate evidence from one plant are insufficient.

An independently allowed nonsharing plant row shows name/link and **Not shared**, with no protected state/reason/value or denominator/support credit. Missing evidence for a sharing plant remains Unknown, not zero, failed or healthy. Real observed zero remains observed zero. Only known observed values enter the substantive denominator, labeled with available-evidence scope; two Unknown plants cannot manufacture a substantive pattern. Singletons can retain their authorized bounded lens row without a pattern.

Whole portfolio is the selected organization's independently deduplicated eligible cohort. Country is a separate actual-country grouping. US Region means one correctable primary official metro/micro CBSA code/type/release, starting July2023/OMB23-01; multistate Regions remain intact while state groups use actual state. Unresolved geography can still contribute to eligible known larger levels/Whole portfolio. No foreign data, census-wide benchmark, street address, coordinates, additional consent or anonymity claim enters this rubric.

## Finding rules

### NIR-01 · Recurring shared concern

Released organization-facing structured PI concern with stable concern_key and lens_key; all source-category grants passed. For a fixed concern_key, count distinct eligible plants with that actual released concern. At least two support a pattern; no diagnosis is invented from a label.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, observed_lens_count, support_count / observed_lens_count when denominator > 0. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants share this recorded {concern_key} concern among {observed_lens_count} plants with available shared evidence for this lens.”

Suggested next step: Offer an organization support conversation about this recorded launch-progress concern; leave cause and pastoral judgment to humans.

### NIR-02 · Recurring shared strength

Released organization-facing structured strength with stable lens_key and strength_key; current eligible evidence. At least two distinct eligible plants have the same actual shared strength_key. Unknown/not_shared never count as a strength.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, observed_lens_count, support_count / observed_lens_count when denominator > 0. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants have a shared {strength_key} strength in the available evidence. A conversation may help the organization learn what they found useful.”

Suggested next step: Offer a voluntary exchange of recorded operational practice through authorized plant links; do not infer transferability, qualifications or guaranteed outcomes.

### NIR-03 · Near-launch preparation support

Actual uncompleted launch status/date plus deterministically unresolved assignment or required-training gap, with full underlying category provenance. For each eligible plant, 0 <= plant-local days_to_launch <= 30 AND (known unfilled required responsibility count > 0 OR known outstanding applicable required training obligations > 0). At least two qualifying distinct plants support the pattern. Near date alone does not qualify; missing gap/date is Unknown.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, observed_launch_preparation_count, support_count / observed_launch_preparation_count when denominator > 0. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants within 30 calendar days of an uncompleted launch have a recorded assignment or required-training gap.”

Suggested next step: Coordinate a bounded preparation support conversation with the affected authorized plants. Do not move dates, change phase, fill roles or claim launch failure.

### NIR-04 · Follow-up ownership support

Shared aggregates of actual live originating-meeting follow-up obligations/tasks: overdue_count and unowned_overdue_count, actual local due dates; all underlying categories allowed. At least two eligible distinct plants have observed overdue_count > 0. A separate unowned subclaim requires at least two distinct plants with unowned_overdue_count > 0. Completion/contact/waiver are distinct.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, sum_overdue_obligations, unowned_support_count only when >=2, sum_unowned_overdue_obligations only when unowned_support_count >=2. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants have {sum_overdue_obligations} recorded overdue follow-up obligations in the available shared evidence.”

Suggested next step: Offer help reviewing existing task ownership and overdue obligations; do not blame a person or claim unsuccessful contact from task status.

### NIR-05 · Genuine-acquisition momentum support

Known valid first-adult-acquisition clock from historical genuine acquisitions, independently of current headcount; uncertainty/provenance carried. Generate stalled theme only with at least two eligible distinct plants whose confirmed clock >=28 days. Generate slowed theme only with at least two whose confirmed clock is >=21 and <28 days. Do not double count stalled plants in slowed theme. Unresolved possible newer acquisition prevents old-date negative claim.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, observed_growth_clock_count, support_count / observed_growth_clock_count when denominator > 0. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants show {momentum_label} in their available first-adult-acquisition evidence as of {as_of}.”

Suggested next step: Offer an operational growth conversation using the recorded timing; do not call a church unhealthy, forecast acquisition, infer conversions or erase genuine acquisitions after withdrawal.

### NIR-06 · Required-training coordination

Saved current required person/program assignments and earned/revoked/corrected completion aggregates, required_applicability_known and nonempty obligation_count. At least two eligible distinct plants with complete applicability evidence and outstanding_required_count > 0 support the pattern. Current roster is explicit, not recalculated from membership. Missing/empty applicability is Unknown, never 100%.

Permitted numerical claims: support_count, sum_outstanding_required_obligations, sum_applicable_required_obligations, sum_current_complete_required_obligations / sum_applicable_required_obligations only for identical reported observed cohort with denominator > 0. Each uses exact persisted aggregate/window/citation.

Example template: “{support_count} plants have {sum_outstanding_required_obligations} outstanding saved required-training obligations in the available shared evidence.”

Suggested next step: Offer coordination around existing assigned programs; no automatic assignment, completion, role qualification or phase effect.

## Evidence and output

All numbers, dates and proportions come from persisted deterministic aggregate facts. A citation binds exact org/group/run, fact path/value, numerator/denominator/formula, source/reference generation, time window and as-of. If a required path/value/support/window cannot be verified, reject the draft before publication. Percent display may round to one decimal but never creates a readiness pass or a missing denominator. No growth cap, forecast or conversion claim is part of v1.

The judge receives aggregate facts, availability, rule results and this whole rubric. Server-only provenance proves contributor support. The server attaches only currently allowed plant name, shared lens state, short reason from an actually shared structured finding and canonical authorized link. An aggregate number already inside a shared reason may remain; a new numeric pattern claim uses an organization/group citation. No per-plant metric table, raw assessments, individual people/interviews/4Cs, source composition, private notes or private-care content/existence/history/calendar/nudge metadata reaches prompts/results/evaluation. Names and links are allowed bounded product fields; they are not raw roster or access grants.

Unknown output says what evidence is available and what is missing. “No supported pattern” never means the portfolio is healthy. A near launch date alone does not warn; a task tick does not prove contact; a real withdrawal never erases a genuine acquisition; incomplete/empty training applicability is not complete. Suggested actions remain operational conversations or existing reviewed workflows, with no automatic task/message/phase/role change or cause assigned to a person. All eligible finding records are retained in stable rule/group/key order, and a compact UI can paginate. Plant rows are never ranked.

## Activation, feedback and verification

[Network examples](network-examples.json) pin synthetic inputs, exact rule/support/group outputs, uncertainty and forbidden-field expectations. Static reference validation can check hashes, rule arithmetic and expected contributor sets; it is separate from future model semantic evaluation. WP041 owns immutable authored content, WP042 evaluates it, WP043 shares the bounded assessment demand/lease/publication machinery, WP047 supplies exact-org projections and WP044/073/074 render/read/review writes. Model/provider/scheduler proof executes later.

A candidate is active only after complete reference-generation validation and explicit publisher activation; failed candidates leave the prior active pointer intact. Rollback is a new activation pointing to prior validated immutable bytes, never rewritten history. Feedback belongs to the actual authorized reader and exact org/run/finding/rubric version; it does not automatically change criteria, scores, models or activation. Every durable Evry action uses exact human review. Current grants are rechecked at publication and every current/history/export/cache/tool/link read. Revocation withholds obsolete contributed patterns immediately; a stale label alone grants nothing.

    "The final C12 ruling is a biweekly 14-day cadence target with predictable rhythm; watch at 21/direct at 28. Earlier open-parameter/change-log text is historical. Weekly predictable practice is legitimate, never overmeeting.",

    "Current known committed-adult size is a deduplicated active adult lower bound with complete/partial/unavailable evidence. Household/stage/account/role/team data proves neither adulthood nor commitment.",

Slowed only at 21 or more days and stalled only at 28 or more days with sufficient timing certainty.",
    "Current actual contact freshness comes from dated effective contacted outcome, never person.updatedAt/task completion/email opens. Missing/manual origin is unmeasured.",

Prelaunch Vision metric, Launch named guest links or debrief cannot substitute. Phase 6 has no exit criterion; add no services module or automatic follow-up generator.",
    "Eight methodology responsibilities are separately mapped to stable actual role assignments; optional imported tenant teams are not mandatory configuration. Prayer Leader is separate coverage, never proof of Prayer lens or ninth conjunction. Phase 1 named agreed worship attestation or actual assignment suffices; Phase 2 all eight needs actual coverage.",
    "Training uses saved explicit required person/program assignments with current earned/revoked/corrected completions, not current team membership/committed adult/headcount/completion-only denominator. Required empty/missing applicability is Unknown; 100 percent means every actual applicable obligation complete, never rounded display.",
    "Candidate conversation requires dated 60 days of unbroken attendance AND volunteering, using dated records/typed planter person attestation with sustained period. Tenure/lifetime counts insufficient. Use only presence/count/date of recorded human interview/FourCs evidence; exclude raw judgments/scores/notes/results from all PI/Evry/model purposes. Infer no qualification, role or promotion. Candidate identities remain planter-only.",
    "Seven legacy attestations stay separate. Prayer rhythms/gatherings/giving each retain own 30-day age/reaffirmation; aged answer stays attributed/aged, not false/current. Funding/systems/values/Prayer Leader keep source nonexpiry. Current criterion values-document evidence, real external relationship, worship agreement, chosen area and executed promotion are explicitly typed separate current operational facts.",

tasks.name: Discernment & Preparation
tasks.description: The work that happens before anyone is gathered — prayer, ground work and the commitments this plant will ask for.

items.title: Write a one-page vision summary
items.description: Who this church is for, what it will be like, and why here. One page — it has to survive being read aloud.

items.title: List the people already praying for this plant
Meet a potential coach
Walk the neighbourhood and write down what you see
Agree the commitments this plant will ask of your family
Draft a budget for the first year

tasks.name: Vision Meeting Preparation
tasks.description: Everything between setting a vision meeting date and standing up to give the talk.

items.title: Set the vision meeting date and time
Write the invitation list
Confirm the venue
Send the invitations
Arrange childcare for the meeting
Prepare the vision talk
Print response cards and name tags
Arrange refreshments
Confirm attendance by phone
items.description: A text is an invitation; a call is a commitment. Ring everyone who said yes.

items.title: Set the room up and rehearse the talk

tasks.name: Post-Meeting Follow-Up
tasks.description: The week after a vision meeting, where interest either becomes a core group or evaporates.

items.title: Record attendance and response cards
Send a thank-you message to everyone who came
Call everyone who said yes
Call everyone who was undecided
Note why anyone declined
Book one-to-one coffees with the interested
Move everyone to their real status in the pipeline

tasks.name: Core Group Onboarding
tasks.description: Turning a list of interested people into a core group that meets, prays and gives.

items.title: Share the vision document with the core group
Set the weekly core group gathering
Agree the core group covenant
Ask each member where they want to serve
Start the giving conversation with the core group
Pray through the launch team names together

tasks.name: Ministry Team Setup
tasks.description: Deciding which teams launch day needs, and putting a name against each one.

items.title: Name the launch coordinator
Decide which ministry teams launch day needs
Name a leader for each ministry team
Write a one-paragraph description for each team
Ask core group members to pick a team
Hold the first ministry team leaders meeting
Agree how often each team meets
Put every team meeting on the shared calendar
Review the team gaps and recruit for them

tasks.name: Launch Date Planning
tasks.description: Choosing the Sunday everything else counts down to, and telling everyone who needs to know.

items.title: Pick a target launch Sunday
Check the date against school and local calendars
Confirm the venue is free on that date
Work backwards and set the preview service dates
Tell the core group the launch date
Tell the sending church and network
Record the launch date in EveryField
items.description: The countdown, the milestones and the oversight announcement all hang off this one date.

tasks.name: Project Timeline Creation
tasks.description: Milestones, owners and the review rhythm that keeps the plan honest.

items.title: List every milestone between now and launch
Put an owner on each milestone
Agree the weekly planning rhythm
Set a monthly budget review
Write down what "ready to launch" means
Review the timeline with your coach

tasks.name: Peak Performance Classes
tasks.description: Booking, filling and running the Peak Performance class series with the core group.

items.title: Book the class dates
Invite the core group to the classes
Order the class materials
Arrange the room and childcare
Run session one
Collect feedback after the first session
Follow up with anyone who missed a session

tasks.name: Ministry Team Training
tasks.description: Every team trained on what it will actually do on a Sunday, and a record of who was there.

items.title: Write the training plan for each team
Book the team training dates
Prepare the worship team run sheet
Train the children's ministry team on safeguarding
items.description: Nothing about launch day is more expensive to get wrong. Checks and ratios included.

items.title: Train greeters and ushers on the welcome flow
Train the setup and teardown team on the room plan
Train the tech team on sound and slides
Run a combined all-teams training
Record who completed each training

tasks.name: Small Group Leader Training
tasks.description: The model, the material and the first leaders — trained before launch, not after it.

items.title: Decide the small group model
Choose the first study material
Identify the first small group leaders
Run leader training session one
Run leader training session two
Assign each leader someone to report to
Set the small group start date

tasks.name: Promotion Campaign
tasks.description: Getting the launch Sunday in front of the neighbourhood, on paper and on screens.

items.title: Agree the promotion budget
Design the invite card
Order the printed invite cards
Build the launch page on the website
Set up the social media accounts
Write four weeks of social posts
Hand invite cards to the launch team
Run the neighbourhood invite drop
Send the local press release
Post the final week reminder

tasks.name: Pre-Launch Services
tasks.description: Preview services, and the debriefs that make the next one better.

items.title: Set the preview service dates
Book the venue for each preview service
Run preview service one
Debrief preview service one
Fix what the debrief found
Run preview service two
Debrief preview service two

tasks.name: Final Preparation
tasks.description: The last checks before launch week, in the order they bite.

items.title: Confirm every team has the people it needs
Confirm the venue contract and access times
Walk the room and mark the setup plan
Test the sound and video in the room
Print the launch day run sheet
Prepare the welcome pack for guests
Confirm childcare ratios and background checks
Brief every team leader on the run sheet
Rest the day before launch

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Setup & Teardown
tasks.description: The trailer, the room and the load-out — the list the setup team works from on the day.

items.title: Load the trailer the night before
Arrive and unload
Set the stage and seating
Check every power run and cable cover
Teardown and load out
Return the room to the state you found it in

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Signage & Parking
tasks.description: Everything that gets a stranger from the main road to a seat.

items.title: Place the road signs
Brief the parking team
Mark the guest parking bays
Place the entrance and welcome signs
Place the children's check-in signs
Collect every sign after the service

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Greeters & Ushers
tasks.description: The first ninety seconds of a guest's experience.

items.title: Brief the greeters on the welcome flow
Set the door positions
Stock and staff the welcome table
Put guest cards and pens on every seat
Agree how latecomers are seated
Hand the completed guest cards to assimilation

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Children's Ministry
tasks.description: Check-in, ratios and safety — the part of launch day that has no acceptable failure.

items.title: Confirm every children's volunteer and their checks
Test the check-in and pick-up system
Set the children's rooms
Lay out the lesson supplies and snacks
Post the allergy and emergency plan in every room
Clear the rooms and log the attendance

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Worship Team
tasks.description: Set list, sound check and the run from call time to close.

items.title: Send the final set list to the band
Build and proof the lyric slides
Confirm the call time with every musician
Run the sound check
Rehearse the full service order
Pack down the stage and instruments

tasks.name: Launch Sunday: Assimilation
tasks.description: What happens to a guest's card between Sunday lunchtime and Tuesday morning.

items.title: Prepare the guest packs
Brief the assimilation team on the follow-up promise
Collect every guest card after the service
Enter each guest into EveryField the same day
Send the thank-you message to every guest
Invite each guest to a next step

tasks.name: First 90 Days Rhythms
tasks.description: The repeating work that turns a launch into a church: guests, leaders, money and the next group.

items.title: Set the weekly service planning meeting
Agree the 48-hour first-time guest follow-up standard
Set the monthly leaders meeting
Set the monthly giving and expenses review
Book the three-month review with your coach
Start the next small group
Plan the first baptism service

roles.description: Primary visionary leader responsible for preaching, vision casting, and shepherding the church plant
Assists the Senior Pastor with pastoral duties, counseling, and leadership development

teams.description: Project management, timeline, milestones, budget tracking, meeting coordination

roles.description: Manages the overall launch timeline, milestones, budget tracking, and meeting coordination
Supports the Launch Coordinator with scheduling, communications, and documentation

teams.description: Worship ministry development, production oversight, musician development, setup/teardown

roles.description: Leads worship ministry development, selects songs, develops musicians, oversees production
Provides vocals during worship services, attends rehearsals
Provides percussion during worship services
Provides bass guitar during worship services
Provides acoustic or electric guitar during worship services
Provides keyboard or piano accompaniment during worship services
Manages audio equipment, mixing, and sound quality during services
Operates presentation software for song lyrics and announcements
Coordinates stage setup, transitions, and equipment management
Coordinates the setup and teardown of worship equipment before and after services

teams.description: Curriculum, volunteer screening, safety protocols, check-in systems, room setup

roles.description: Oversees all children's ministry operations, curriculum, safety protocols, and volunteer management
Manages nursery operations for infants and toddlers during services
Leads preschool-age programming and classroom management
Leads elementary-age programming, lessons, and activities
Manages the child check-in and check-out system for safety and security
Ensures all safety protocols are followed, manages background checks and training compliance
Selects, prepares, and distributes curriculum materials for all age groups

teams.description: Secure worship site, manage venue relationship, signage, parking, storage

roles.description: Oversees venue relationship, facility logistics, and coordinates all facilities teams
Coordinates the pre-service setup of all areas including seating, signage, and equipment
Coordinates post-service teardown, cleanup, and equipment storage
Manages parking logistics, directional signage, and parking lot greeting
Creates and places directional and welcome signage for services and events
Manages storage unit or area, equipment inventory, and supply ordering

teams.description: Guest tracking, follow-up process, Friendship Registers, data management, Guest Reception, Party with the Pastor, Peak Performance classes

roles.description: Oversees the complete guest assimilation process from first visit through full integration
Manages the Guest Reception area, greets first-time visitors, and collects connection information
Manages the follow-up process for all guests within 48 hours of their visit
Enters guest information from Friendship Registers and connection cards into the system
Plans and executes Party with the Pastor events for prospective members
Coordinates Peak Performance class scheduling, registration, and materials

teams.description: Leader identification and training, Small Group 101, group assignment, Apprentice Program, curriculum

roles.description: Oversees the Small Groups ministry, identifies and trains leaders, manages curriculum
Mentors and supports multiple small group leaders, ensures group health
Facilitates a small group, provides pastoral care for group members
Learning to lead a small group through the Apprentice Program under a current leader

teams.description: Marketing plan, social media, press releases, direct mail, invitation materials

roles.description: Develops and executes the marketing plan, coordinates all promotional activities
Manages social media accounts, creates content, engages with followers
Creates visual materials including flyers, banners, social media graphics, and branding
Manages print production of invitations, mailers, bulletins, and other materials

teams.description: Prayer strategy, prayer teams, corporate prayer events, communication of requests

roles.description: Develops prayer strategy, organizes corporate prayer events, manages prayer teams
Leads a prayer team, coordinates prayer assignments, and facilitates prayer meetings
Manages the prayer chain, distributes prayer requests, and coordinates responses

teams.description: Website development, production technology, assimilation software, communication tools

roles.description: Oversees all technology systems including website, production tech, and church software
Manages church website content, updates, hosting, and online presence
Manages audio/visual equipment, live streaming, and production technology
Manages church database systems, data integrity, and reporting

documents.name: Core Group Commitment Card
documents.description: A print-ready quarter-page card founding members sign to commit to GROW, PRAY, and GIVE through Launch Sunday.

documents.name: Response Card
documents.description: A quarter-page card guests complete at a vision meeting to share contact info and how they'd like to be involved.

documents.name: Guest Sign-in Sheet
documents.description: A letter-size sheet for capturing names, contact info, and who invited each guest at a vision meeting.

documents.name: Vision Meeting Agenda
documents.description: A one-page agenda to keep a vision meeting on track — welcome, story, vision, GROW/PRAY/GIVE ask, and next steps.

documents.name: Expectations of a Core Group Member
documents.description: An editable one-pager spelling out what's expected of a founding core-group member — presence, GROW/PRAY/GIVE, and team participation.

documents.name: Launch Team Commitment
documents.description: An editable commitment letter launch-team members sign as the plant moves toward Launch Sunday.

documents.name: Vision Meeting Follow-up Letter
documents.description: An editable letter to send guests after a vision meeting — thank them, keep the connection warm, and invite the next step.

documents.name: Board / Elder Meeting Agenda
documents.description: An editable agenda for a board or elder meeting — prayer, minutes, financials, ministry updates, and action items.

documents.name: First-Year Budget
documents.description: A 12-month budget spreadsheet with income/expense categories and live total formulas.

documents.name: Budget Worksheet
documents.description: A simple monthly-vs-annual budget planner spreadsheet with live total formulas.

documents.name: Launch Sunday Checklists
documents.description: A print-ready packet with a per-team launch-day checklist — setup, hospitality, worship, kids, connections, and prayer.

launch.title: Set-up equipment on site
launch.description: Every piece of set-up equipment needed to launch arrives during the three-to-four week window, stored and labelled.

tasks.title: Order the remaining set-up equipment
Confirm delivery dates for everything still outstanding
Label and store the equipment where the team will find it

launch.title: Set-up and tear-down training held
launch.description: A full Saturday of in-service training: hands-on set-up and tear-down, storage, care of equipment, and working as teams.

tasks.title: Book the full-Saturday in-service training
Walk the team through set-up, tear-down and storage
Test and improve Worship Center acoustics and lighting

launch.title: Worship Center secured and rehearsed in
launch.description: The room is secured for set-up, tear-down and launch-team meetings — optimally used three times before Launch Sunday.

tasks.title: Confirm the Worship Center booking
Schedule three uses of the room before Launch Sunday

launch.title: Prayer and fasting underway
launch.description: One day a week of fasting through the four weeks before launch, ending in corporate worship, prayer and a shared meal. The senior pastor leads it.

tasks.title: Set the weekly fast day for the four weeks before launch
Plan the worship, prayer and shared meal that close each fast

launch.title: Three pre-launch services held
launch.description: Launch-team-only services on the three Sundays (or Saturdays) before launch: set-up, worship, preaching, children's ministry, assimilation, celebration.

tasks.title: Book the Worship Center for three pre-launch services
Run pre-launch service 1
Run pre-launch services 2 and 3

launch.title: Ministry training 90–100% complete
launch.description: Specific ministry training should be all but finished before the final window — this is the time to integrate the parts into the whole.

tasks.title: Finish children's ministry training: teachers, curriculum, check-in, safety
Finish the worship team run-through
Test assimilation end to end

launch.title: Promotion plan chosen
launch.description: A well-thought-out, prayerful plan sized to the plant's financial condition — not every channel in the Playbook, the right ones.

tasks.title: Choose the promotion channels your budget supports
Set the launch team's personal invitation goal

launch.title: Promotion plan implemented
launch.description: Three to four weeks out triggers the full launch of the promotion plan — get the word out by every means the plan named.

tasks.title: Send the press release to local media
Run the email blast and social posts
Distribute invitation cards, door hangers and mailers

launch.title: Partner churches announcing the launch
launch.description: The week before launch, every partner church shows the announcement slide — and the partner organization's role in the service is settled.

tasks.title: Email the launch announcement slide to every partner church
Confirm the partner organization's role in the service
